title: Eight-unit-cell electronic modulations in cuprates originating from local molecular orbitals
authors: Zhiheng Yao, Sixuan Chen, Jianfa Zhao, Shusen Ye, Weixiang Qu, Ning Xia, Yuling Dai, Luchuan Shi, Hongrui Zhang, Zhenqi Hao, Changqing Jin, Shuo Yang, Yayu Wang
abstract: The pair density wave (PDW) state with eight-unit-cell (8a0) periodicity has been widely regarded as the primary order in cuprates, yet its existence and origin remain subjects of intense debate. Using spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy, we observe spatial modulations of the electronic states with approximately 8a0 periodicity in both the superconducting and insulating regimes of hole-doped Ca2CuO2Cl2 cuprate. We find that the 8a0 spatial patterns are generated by the formation of molecular orbitals by doped holes, which organize into 4a0*4a0 plaquettes as the basic unit. Our results identify the 4a0 molecular orbital as the fundamental electronic building block in cuprates, while the 8a0 PDW represents a spatial subharmonic that emerges at sufficiently high doping.
summary: This research uses STM and theoretical modeling to argue that the prominent eight-unit-cell electronic modulation in cuprates is not a conventional pair density wave, but rather a spatial subharmonic. This modulation arises from the self-assembly of local electronic states into fundamental four-unit-cell plaquettes, establishing the plaquette as the primary electronic building block.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nature and origin of the eight-unit-cell (8a0) electronic modulation observed in cuprate superconductors, challenging the conventional view of the pair density wave (PDW).
main_result: The 8a0 modulation is proposed to be a spatial subharmonic arising from the self-organization of local molecular orbitals, which are fundamentally built from $4a_0 	imes 4a_0$ plaquettes, rather than a simple finite-momentum pairing instability.
method: The study combines spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) experiments with theoretical modeling using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations.
model_or_system: The system is hole-doped cuprates ($	ext{Ca}_2	ext{CuO}_2	ext{Cl}_2$), modeled using a statistical framework where the elementary degree of freedom is the $4a_0$ plaquette, governed by interaction energies between nearest-neighbor plaquettes.
key_observables: Spatial modulations with $8a_0$ periodicity, $4a_0$ plaquettes, and the correlation between these modulations and internal stripe patterns.
important_parameters: Doping levels ($p=0.03, p=0.05, p=0.10$), temperature ($T$), and interaction parameters ($g_\alpha, g_ eta, W$).
main_assumptions: The $4a_0$ plaquette is the fundamental electronic building block, and the $8a_0$ modulation originates from the depletion regions separating these plaquettes.
figures_summary: Figures show STM $	ext{d}I/	ext{d}V$ maps and Fourier transform analyses confirming $4a_0$ and $8a_0$ modulations in both superconducting and insulating regimes, alongside MCMC simulations reproducing these periodicity peaks.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental observation of $8a_0$ modulations in STM to proposing the $4a_0$ plaquette as the basic unit, and finally developing and testing a statistical model (MCMC) to confirm that the $8a_0$ periodicity is a geometric consequence of the plaquette arrangement.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, real-space mechanism (molecular orbital self-organization) to explain a key feature of high-Tc superconductivity, offering a potential alternative to purely momentum-space descriptions of pairing order.

FIG. 4. Monte Carlo simulation illustrating the emergence of 8a0 modulations from the self- organization of 4a0 molecular orbitals. (a) Impurity potential generated by randomly distributed dopants for p = 0.05. (b) Representative low-temperature configurations of 4a0 plaquettes, showing the formation of plaquette chains. (c) The line profiles along the corresponding FT (inset), revealing the dominant 4a0 periodicity and the accompanying 8a0 modulation. (d) to (f) The same set of results as in (a)-(c) for p = 0.10. The plaquette chains become longer because of the increased coverage of molecular orbitals. Both the 4a0 and 8a0 periodicities are clearly observed.
